parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no state-imposed birth-sex facility rule, and foreign documents are not documented as rejected — so no tier-1 universal exposure and no organised state targeting. Strong, working recourse: national sex-discrimination protection since 2013, an August 2024 ruling awarding damages against a service that excluded a trans woman, fresh hate-crime coverage (Feb 2025), and an apprehended-violence order protecting a targeted trans woman — evidence remedies operate, not just paper. Detention standards in the one documented state place prisoners by lived gender (staff discretion, surgery exception). Offsets: documented organised exclusionary campaigns and facility/records disputes (social hostility, not state threat-framing), no prosecution data, dated 2003 document-marker and assault evidence, and a subnational patchwork where three states omit gender identity and two omit both. Broad social acceptance is asserted only weakly. Above the 0.65 tier, below the 0.75–0.85 anchors that document consistent acceptance.
